newsitem.title: UK: Eurostocks mixed, dollar up on US rate prospects.
newsitem.headline: Eurostocks mixed, dollar up on US rate prospects.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Monday as worries took hold that the United States would increase interest rates for the first time in two years -- a prospect that boosted the dollar.

London and Paris slipped but Frankfurt gained with investors keeping a wary eye out for Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee, widely expected to raise rates.
The expectations of higher interest rates squeezed the dollar upwards by nearly a pfennig and half a yen by midday as traders anticipated a more attractive return on dollar-denominated assets.

London equities suffered the most from the interest rates jitters although markets on both sides of the Atlantic saw volatile trading last week after hints by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.

London's FTSE index of leading shares was down 0.5 percent, the sixth consecutive trading session to register losses, for a total of nearly four percent. At one point, the index was down 29.2.points to 4,225.6, the lowest level in almost two months.

"I was surprised to see us get those levels," said one senior dealer of the early bounce. "There's anxiety ahead of the FOMC meeting tomorrow, there's anxiety about UK interest rates and there's anxiety about the election."
In contrast, Frankfurt moved ahead by 0.7 percent as investors shrugged off the rates worries and instead took comfort from the stronger dollar, seen as good news for the exporting sector.
"The market is surprisingly strong this morning. .. the main factor is that the market has factored in a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," said a Frankfurt trader.

As bourse trade in Frankfurt opened, the focus was on Thyssen AG , which was up 19 marks, or 4.86 percent at 410 marks, rising on reports it was planning to tell shareholders that its shares have the potential to reach a price of around 550 marks.
Last week Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch announced a takeover bid. Since then Thyssen has agreed to discuss a joint steel company. If the talks fail, Krupp said it planned to reinstate the offer.
In Paris, shares climbed at the opening but fell later in the session as the market focused attention on the FOMC meeting and optimism ebbed away.
Among individual stocks, Lyonnaise des Eaux rose 2.67 percent to 576 francs and Suez was up 2.4 percent at 287.10 following newspaper reports the two were preparing a merger.
On the currency front, the dollar was trading more strongly with analysts also predicting a 25 basis point hike in the key Fed funds rate at Tuesday's FOMC meeting.

"A 25 basis point hike has already been priced in... The increase we're looking for tomorrow would be seen as the first of a number of increases," said Julian Fisher, international economist at Daiwa Europe in London.
But a discordant note for the dollar was struck by a senior Bundesbank official who expressed concern about the effect a U.S. rate hike would have on German rates.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said an increase in U.S. rates could push German rates higher, adding that this "cannot be desirable". He said the central bank considered the level of German rates appropriate now in view of current inflation, the economic situation, and money supply.

"The (Welteke) comments... were slightly deutschemark-supportive, but the main backdrop is dollar-supportive based on the expectations of higher interest rates tomorrow," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6905 marks and 122.93 yen compared with 1.6835 marks and 122.55 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 24.2 points at 4,230.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.47 points at 2,582.66.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 23.70 points at 3,321.94.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $350.65 an ounce, against London's close of $352.65 on Friday. Silver was at $5.13, down five cents.
